quote: the cost of electricity has skyrocketed, that kind of thing, in Virginia.
stewart_read: Customer hands the rep a clear pain-point reason (rising electricity costs) but the rep never reflects it back or ties it to the appointment later — it's filed and dropped.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep could be intentionally deferring emotional framing to the specialist since no bill exists yet to anchor against.
coaching_implication: Even without a bill, rep could say 'that rising-cost trend is exactly why we're getting your design ready before you move in' to keep the reason alive.

quote: I have no clue. I I don't close on my house till Friday.
stewart_read: No bill exists because the customer hasn't moved in — this is a legitimate non-standard case correctly handled by skipping bill_collection rather than forcing it.
coaching_implication: Correct handling; rep should still flag this account for bill follow-up once customer is in the home so paid-lead bill capture isn't permanently skipped.

quote: my job is just to get you qualified and make sure everything makes sense
stewart_read: Rep explicitly holds setter scope, deferring design and equipment questions to the specialist rather than improvising numbers.
coaching_implication: This is the escape-hatch language the schema wants — worth using as a positive exemplar for other reps.

quote: So Thursday, I'll be busy I mean, you know, like I said, I'm not stationed there yet.
stewart_read: First proposed date fails because rep didn't first confirm the move timeline before offering Thursday, forcing a second and third round of negotiation.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep may have offered Thursday deliberately as a null test to surface the real constraint faster — but no evidence he planned this.
coaching_implication: Ask about move-in date before proposing a day to avoid burning two extra rounds of back-and-forth.

quote: I get so much so many, like, random ass phone calls, you know, that I don't answer.
stewart_read: Customer raises a legitimacy/spam-screening concern at the very end; rep resolves it with a concrete promise (texting the specialist's actual number) rather than a vague reassurance.
coaching_implication: Good micro-trade — swap a vague promise for a specific mechanism. Worth reinforcing as the standard move for this concern.

quote: is it an opportunity for me to, you know, invest in solar since we're gonna be there for a couple of years and, you know, hopefully, save some money?
stewart_read: Customer unprompted frames solar as an investment opportunity tied to a multi-year stay — a strong buy-in signal.
coaching_implication: Rep should have echoed this back at booking ('since you're planning to be there a few years, this is exactly the kind of home worth designing for') to reinforce motivation into the appointment.
